display_name: Bhima I & Kumarapala of Chaulukya Gujarat
one_line: Chaulukya kings of Gujarat linked in tradition to the destruction and rebuilding phases of the Somnath shrine and its recovering pilgrimage economy.

appearance.age_look: Bhima I appears in his late 30s with a sturdy, broad-shouldered build; Kumarapala appears in his mid-40s with a slightly leaner but still regal frame.
appearance.face: Bhima I has a square face, medium-brown complexion, strong jaw, straight nose, thick brows and a calm, resolute default expression; Kumarapala has an oval face, slightly lighter wheat-brown complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache and a contemplative, composed default expression.
appearance.hair: Bhima I’s black hair is pulled back into a tight, medium-height topknot bound with a simple gold band, with short sideburns; Kumarapala’s black hair is similarly tied in a slimmer topknot but mostly hidden by a small, rounded golden Gujarati-style crown with a low central peak and a narrow red cloth band at its base.
appearance.costume: Bhima I wears a knee-length, off-white cotton angarkha-style tunic with a wrapped front and side-tie, over a deep-red dhoti tied in the Gujarati style, pleated to mid-calf, with a narrow golden border; over his shoulder is a plain indigo cotton uparna (shawl) with a subtle woven check pattern, and he has a broad leather belt at his waist holding a small pouch; his jewellery is modest—simple gold stud earrings, a single flat gold necklace, and a thin armlet on each upper arm; his sandals are brown leather with toe loops. Kumarapala wears a more elaborate cream-coloured silk angarkha with fine golden edging and a slightly flared skirt reaching the knees, paired with a pale-green silk dhoti with broader gold borders, also in Gujarati wrap; he has a rich maroon silk uparna with fine geometric motifs draped neatly over his left shoulder and across the chest; his jewellery includes a layered but not ostentatious gold necklace with small pendants, medium-sized circular gold earrings, a single finely worked armlet on his right upper arm, and a slim ring on his right hand; his sandals are darker brown leather, slightly more refined in finish.
appearance.signature: Bhima I holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a red cord in his left hand and a simple wooden measuring rod in his right as symbols of temple rebuilding and planning, while Kumarapala carries a small, ornamented copper water pot (kalasha) cradled in his left hand, symbolizing ritual patronage and renewed worship.

ref_desc: Bhima I and Kumarapala stand together, both medium-brown Gujarati kings with black topknots, Bhima in off-white angarkha, deep-red dhoti and indigo shawl holding a palm-leaf manuscript and wooden measuring rod, Kumarapala in cream angarkha, pale-green dhoti, maroon shawl, small gold crown and copper kalasha, all in warm off-white, red, indigo, cream and maroon tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two Chaulukya-era Gujarati kings, Bhima I and Kumarapala, shown together in dignified, historically grounded attire from 11th–12th century Gujarat: Bhima is a sturdy, late-30s man with a square face, medium-brown complexion, strong jaw, thick brows and calm expression, his black hair pulled into a tight medium-height topknot bound with a simple gold band; he wears a knee-length off-white cotton angarkha with wrapped front, a deep-red Gujarati-style dhoti with narrow gold border to mid-calf, an indigo cotton uparna with subtle checks over one shoulder, a broad leather belt with a small pouch, simple gold stud earrings, a single flat gold necklace, thin armlets and brown leather sandals, holding a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied in red in one hand and a plain wooden measuring rod in the other to signify planning the rebuilding of Somnath after its destruction. Beside him, Kumarapala is a slightly leaner mid-40s man with an oval face, wheat-brown complexion, neat moustache and contemplative, composed expression, his black hair tied in a slimmer topknot mostly under a small rounded golden crown with a low central peak and a narrow red cloth band; he wears a cream silk angarkha with fine golden edging and a slightly flared skirt, a pale-green silk Gujarati dhoti with broader gold borders, and a maroon silk uparna with fine geometric motifs draped over his left shoulder and across his chest, with layered but modest gold necklace, medium gold earrings, a single armlet, a slim ring and refined brown leather sandals, holding an ornamented copper kalasha in his left hand as a symbol of temple ritual and patronage; show both characters front-facing, side and back views to capture consistent face shapes, hair, garments, jewellery, weapons/props and the shared warm palette of off-white, deep red, indigo, cream and maroon in a solemn, resilient mood emphasizing economic and spiritual recovery rather than battle.
